pr_title: Add consideration of subpass index when sorting rendering elements
pr_comments: I dont understand the need for this, if you really want materials rendered in specific order, just use the priority property of Material.

> I dont understand the need for this, if you really want materials rendered in specific order, just use the priority property of Material.

A material's subpass should be rendered after itself.
But after some consideration, I think you are right, it cause things complex in fact.

But there is another problem, the sort key here:
https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/c3ea4ea9b76d1bacde83f7b70af4638cf2ff41a2/drivers/gles2/rasterizer_scene_gles2.h#L592-L609

In little endian, for example: 0x12345678 was in fact 0x78563412 in memory, not just reversed bits, so the sort might be wrong in some rare cases.

issue_context.title: Material used as next pass on multiple objects only affects one at a time
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:** 3.1 and 3.2 alpha1

**OS/device including version:** Windows 10; 10.0.18362 Build 18362

**Issue description:**
![example](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/52017025/67524472-5f7b4a00-f676-11e9-94e6-742a6d050403.gif)

I have a pair of MeshInstances, each with their own separate material to start with (green sphere, blue cube) and a SpatialMaterial with the color red.
When I put this spatial material into the next pass slot of each MeshInstance's material, only one of them appears red at a time.

Giving multiple objects the same material resource behaves just fine normally, its just using next pass where this behavior appears...

Maybe this is some kind of intentional limitation, but it seems inconsistent to me, and is a hassle to deal with.

For example, I want to apply the same shader material, with the same uniform settings, to several different objects as an additional pass, but can't do so conveniently because of this. I would have to duplicate the material and individually set the uniforms for each of them. 😢 

The example project puts the materials in the material slot of the MeshInstance, but the same thing occurs when placed in the mesh itself's material slot as well.
Only the editor view is necessary to show this, but it does happen when using a camera in the running game as well.

**Minimal reproduction project:** [minimalrepro.zip](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/files/3769425/minimalrepro.zip)
comments: You can set your maaterial's priority to change materials' sort order

review_comments: This limits the number of shaders you can have from 1024 (already dangerously low) to 256. It might be best to figure out a way to do this without adjusting "sort_key". I tried to fiddle with it once before but reduz didn't allow it. He has planned out these values very carefully.
